reason: This is the only available action, and collisions should begin reshaping the orbiting debris.
expectation: The debris may collide and redistribute, possibly allowing some material to gather into the Moon; the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The collisions spread the debris into a ring, leaving routes outward and back toward Earth.
reaction: The clarification that the disk is not a solid ring is useful.
reason: I’ll follow the outward material toward the region where a Moon can gather.
expectation: Some ring material may move beyond the tidal disruption region, where it can begin to accumulate.

alternatives.reason: This may follow debris falling back to Earth, but I want to pursue the Moon first.

effect: The outward debris has formed moonlets that can survive and merge beyond the disruptive tidal region.
reaction: It is satisfying to see why the location allows clumps to survive.
reason: Continue gathering the moonlets toward the Moon goal.
expectation: Gravity may merge the moonlets into a larger lunar body.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth is also a goal, but I’ll finish the outward route first.

effect: The moonlets have gathered into a hot young Moon, which still needs to cool for the crust goal.
reaction: The progression from debris to a molten satellite is satisfying.
reason: I’ll cool the young Moon to continue toward its crust.
expectation: The Moon will lose heat to space, potentially forming a cooling crust.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth is also a goal, but I want to finish the Moon route first.

effect: Cooling produced lunar minerals; their different densities may help form a crust.
reaction: The distinction between sinking and floating crystals is interesting.
reason: Combine the crystals with the young Moon to continue forming its crust.
expectation: Some crystals may float and accumulate into a lunar crust.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth remains a goal, but I’ll finish the Moon route first.

effect: Buoyant plagioclase has formed a floating layer within the Moon, suggesting further cooling will develop its crust.
reaction: The link between mineral buoyancy and the pale crust is interesting.
reason: Continue cooling the floating layer to finish the lunar crust.
expectation: The layer may cool and solidify into a lunar crust.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth is still needed, but I’ll finish the Moon route first.

effect: The Moon now has an early pale crust, completing that goal; returning debris to Earth remains.
reaction: The reminder that the familiar dark maria have not formed yet is useful.
reason: Follow the only offered combination to return the remaining debris toward Earth.
expectation: Gravity may draw some of the spreading ring inward toward Earth, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The inward-moving debris is falling back toward Earth rather than joining the Moon.
reaction: The split between the debris’s two paths is clear.
reason: The only offered combination should return the falling rock to the surviving Earth.
expectation: The rock will rejoin Earth, adding material and energy and likely completing the remaining goal.

effect: The falling debris rejoined and reheated Earth, completing the remaining goal while leaving some acquired volatiles with the planet.
reaction: The return path gives the debris a meaningful consequence beyond forming the Moon.

mostWorthwhile.text: Forming the floating feldspar-rich layer made the connection between mineral buoyancy and the Moon’s pale crust clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final return-to-Earth sequence was clear but felt somewhat predictable, with only one combination offered at each step.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that the Moon’s pale early crust formed from buoyant crystals and did not yet have the familiar dark maria.

arbitrary.text: Combining crystals with the young Moon could sound like adding material from outside, but the result clarified that the layer forms within the Moon.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the remade Earth develops, especially since the chapter connected its reaccreted debris to renewed heating.
